text: Actual Monero mining by a Frothly endpoint would be evidenced in the available data by mining-service DNS queries and matching outbound network connections from covered endpoints, and the searched endpoint-to-network feeds cover the candidate Frothly endpoints well enough to compare them for that behavior.
evidence: index=botsv3 sourcetype=stream:dns | stats dc(query) as distinct_queries, count as events by host returned 16 rows covering all 7 primary Frothly endpoints with 5k-16k DNS events each, so mining-service DNS from any of them would appear in this feed. The 8th endpoint, BGIST-L, has no stream:tcp/http/ip events at all and only WinHostMon coverage (14410 events), in which a search for coinhive/miner/xmrig/monero in Name and CommandLine returned 0 events — no feed that exists for BGIST-L could show or hide mining. Sysmon EventCode=3 additionally covers 8 hosts (ABUNGST-L 1073, BGIST-L 12, BSTOLL-L 16, BTUN-L 31, FYODOR-L 3931, JWORTOS-L 3, MKRAEUS-L 1, PCERF-L 5).
stamp_reason: The cited results support the claim that the searched network feeds and endpoint coverage can evidence actual mining activity: they show endpoint DNS coverage, TCP connection evidence for Coinhive IPs, and the limits of Sysmon/http/BGIST-L coverage.
holds_reason: The strongest rival is that actual Monero mining could be present on another Frothly endpoint in the available data but outside the searched evidence paths. The report addresses this by showing all seven primary endpoints are covered in stream:dns and that BGIST-L's only held feed is WinHostMon with no miner indicators, leaving no better in-scope rival evidenced.

text: BSTOLL-L is the only Frothly endpoint that actually mined Monero because it is the only covered endpoint with Coinhive-related DNS queries and matching outbound connections to the resolved mining-server IPs.
evidence: index=botsv3 (sourcetype=stream:tcp OR sourcetype=stream:http OR sourcetype=stream:ip) (dest_ip IN (37.187.167.47,104.20.209.59,104.20.208.59) OR src_ip IN (...)) returned exactly 2 rows, both from src_ip=192.168.247.131 (BSTOLL-L), connecting to the IPs its coinhive DNS queries resolved to. The all-hosts mining-domain DNS search (coinhive/monero/minergate/nanopool/supportxmr/cryptonight/deepminr/coinweb/minero) returned 6 rows, all host=BSTOLL-L. No other covered endpoint has either the DNS queries or the matching connections, so BSTOLL-L is the only Frothly endpoint that actually mined Monero.
rival: Other covered Frothly endpoints in stream:dns and related network feeds that could have mining-domain queries or matching outbound connections but do not.
stamp_reason: The report's results directly support the claim: BSTOLL-L is the only host shown with Coinhive DNS, matching TCP connections to resolved Coinhive IPs, and concurrent browser CPU saturation, while other covered endpoints lack those indicators.
holds_reason: The strongest rival is another endpoint fitting 'actually mined Monero' as well as BSTOLL-L. The evidence rules that out by showing no other covered endpoint has either the mining-domain DNS or the matching outbound connections, and BGIST-L lacks network telemetry while its only held endpoint feed shows no miner indicators.
